extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and readers of philosophy (particularly aesthetics and Kantian studies)
extracted.subtask_description: Explain and evaluate Kant’s principles for making aesthetic (taste, beauty, sublime) and teleological judgements about nature and art. Covers criteria for purity of taste, universality, purposiveness, genius, and teleology.

rubrics_metrics.name: The judgement of taste is aesthetical
rubrics_metrics.description: “The judgement of taste is aesthetical.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant treats judgements of taste as arising from aesthetic feeling rather than from concepts or determinate cognition; they are evaluations grounded in feeling (see §1).

rubrics_metrics.name: The satisfaction which determines the judgement of taste is disinterested
rubrics_metrics.description: “The satisfaction which determines the judgement of taste is disinterested.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pure judgement of taste requires pleasure independent of personal desire or interest (not about possession or moral good). Anti-pattern: conflating aesthetic pleasure with desire to possess or with practical interest (§2).

rubrics_metrics.name: The satisfaction in the pleasant is bound up with interest
rubrics_metrics.description: “The satisfaction in the pleasant is bound up with interest.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleasure from the merely pleasant depends on sensuous interest and is not a pure aesthetic judgement (§3). Distinguish from disinterested aesthetic pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: The satisfaction in the good is bound up with interest
rubrics_metrics.description: “The satisfaction in the good is bound up with interest.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgements about the morally or practically good are tied to interests and ends, unlike pure aesthetic judgements (§4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of three specifically different kinds of satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative criterion: pleasant vs good vs aesthetic satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant analyses differences among pleasures of sense, practical/moral satisfaction, and disinterested aesthetic pleasure to delimit what counts as a pure judgement of taste (§5).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Beautiful is that which apart from concepts is represented as the object of a universal satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Beautiful is that which apart from concepts is represented as the object of a universal satisfaction.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty claims a kind of universal assent while not resting on a determinate concept; key criterion of aesthetic beauty (§6).

rubrics_metrics.name: The universality of the satisfaction is represented in a judgement of Taste only as subjective
rubrics_metrics.description: “The universality of the satisfaction is represented in a judgement of Taste only as subjective.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although we expect others to agree about beauty, the universality is not a logical/cognitive universal but a subjective expectation grounded in common cognitive faculties (§8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation whether feeling precedes or follows the judging of the object
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether in a judgement of taste the feeling of pleasure precedes or follows the judging of the object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses the temporal/psychological ordering in aesthetic judgement; useful for analyzing whether judgment is inferential or immediate (§9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Of purposiveness in general
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of purposiveness in general.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purposiveness (Zweckmässigkeit) — the appearance of adaptation or fittedness — is the fundamental principle underlying aesthetic judgement (see §10).

rubrics_metrics.name: The judgement of taste has nothing at its basis but the form of the purposiveness of an object
rubrics_metrics.description: “The judgement of taste has nothing at its basis but the form of the purposiveness of an object (or of its mode of representation).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty arises from a perceived formal purposiveness of the object with respect to our cognitive faculties, not from an attributed external purpose (§11).

rubrics_metrics.name: The judgement of taste rests on a priori grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: “The judgement of taste rests on _a priori_ grounds.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant argues for a priori conditions of taste (principles governing the faculty of judgement) even though judgements are not conceptual determinations (§12).

rubrics_metrics.name: The pure judgement of taste is independent of charm and emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: “The pure judgement of taste is independent of charm and emotion.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purity, aesthetic judgement must be free from contingent charms, associations, or strong emotions; presence of such dependent features makes the judgement impure (§13).

rubrics_metrics.name: The judgement of taste is quite independent of the concept of perfection
rubrics_metrics.description: “The judgement of taste is quite independent of the concept of perfection.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty is not simply judged by reference to a concept of perfection; perfection-based pleasure belongs to a different evaluative mode (§15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgement of taste conditional on a definite concept is not pure
rubrics_metrics.description: “The judgement of taste, by which an object is declared to be beautiful under the condition of a definite concept, is not pure.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If beauty is evaluated relative to a concept (e.g., an intended function), that renders the aesthetic judgement dependent, not pure (§16).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Ideal of Beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the Ideal of Beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant distinguishes ideals (conceptual standards) from pure aesthetic judgement; useful when assessing works that appeal to ideals rather than immediate aesthetic form (§17).

rubrics_metrics.name: The modality in a judgement of taste and subjective necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: “What the modality in a judgement of taste is” and “The subjective necessity which we ascribe to the judgement of taste is conditioned.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though we feel that aesthetic judgements carry a necessity (we expect agreement), that necessity is subjective and conditioned (requires presuppositions) (§18–20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of universal agreement presupposes a common sense (sensus communis)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The condition of necessity which a judgement of taste asserts is the Idea of a common sense” and “Have we ground for presupposing a common sense?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant introduces the notion of a sensus communis — shared cognitive faculties — as a presupposition that makes the subjective claim to universality intelligible (§20–21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicability of aesthetic sensation
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the communicability of a sensation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taste presupposes that our aesthetic feelings can be communicated and that others share similar cognitive faculties; this supports claims to universal assent (§39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste as a kind of sensus communis
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of taste as a kind of _sensus communis_.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taste functions as a shared sense enabling mutual aesthetic judgement; this is central to explaining social agreement about beauty (§40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical interest in the Beautiful
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the empirical interest in the Beautiful.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an empirical (subjective) interest that can influence aesthetic judgement; Kant distinguishes this from pure (a priori) taste (§41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual interest in the Beautiful
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the intellectual interest in the Beautiful.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another form of interest — intellectual appreciation — can shape judgements but should be separated from pure aesthetic judgement (§42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Of Art in general and Beautiful Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and analysis of Art and Beautiful Art (e.g., §43–46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant sets criteria distinguishing art from science, and beautiful art as art that seems like nature; useful for judging artworks' aesthetic status (§43–46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful art is an art in so far as it seems like nature
rubrics_metrics.description: “Beautiful art is an art in so far as it seems like nature.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic value of art is tied to how well it mimics or appears natural in form; this is a criterion for evaluating art (§45).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful art is the art of genius
rubrics_metrics.description: “Beautiful art is the art of genius.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genius (innate productive disposition) is the source of true beautiful art; criterion: works exhibiting aesthetic ideas that surpass conceptual explanation indicate genius (§46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius: innate disposition and incommunicable method
rubrics_metrics.description: “Genius is… that innate mental disposition through which Nature gives the rule to Art.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genius cannot fully explain its method; a sign of genius is production of aesthetic ideas that cannot be rendered fully by rules — but taste must regulate genius to avoid violations (§46–50).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of Taste with Genius in works of art
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the combination of Taste with Genius in the products of beautiful Art.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideal artwork combines original genius (aesthetic ideas) with taste (form and restraint); if genius overrides taste, can violate aesthetic canons (§50).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division and combination of the beautiful arts
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the division of the beautiful arts” and “Of the combination of beautiful arts in one and the same product.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant provides criteria for differentiating arts by medium (space/time) and for evaluating multimedia works based on how arts combine (§51–52).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of the respective aesthetical worth of the beautiful arts
rubrics_metrics.description: “Comparison of the respective aesthetical worth of the beautiful arts.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers a framework for ranking arts’ aesthetic value according to their capacity to present aesthetic ideas and engage imagination vs concept (§53).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antinomy/dialectic of Taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation and solution of the antinomy of Taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize tensions and contradictions in claims about universality vs subjectivity in taste; the dialectic examines limits of pretended principles (§55–57).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty as the symbol of Morality
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of Beauty as the symbol of Morality.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant suggests connections between aesthetic disposition and moral feeling; capacity for aesthetic appreciation can be read as a sign of moral sensibility (§59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of Taste (Appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix: Of the method of Taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance for cultivating and applying taste — includes rules, examples, and how to avoid common mistakes in aesthetic judgement (§60, Appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition from judging Beautiful to judging Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: “Transition from the faculty which judges of the Beautiful to that which judges of the Sublime.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets criteria distinguishing restful aesthetic contemplation (beauty) from the movement/excitation associated with the sublime (§23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisions of investigation into feeling of the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the divisions of an investigation into the feeling of the Sublime.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublime divided into mathematically sublime (magnitude) and dynamically sublime (power); each has different evaluative marks (§24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematically Sublime — magnitude and estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematically Sublime: definition and requisite estimation of magnitude for the Idea of the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects that overwhelm our faculty of magnitude estimation (absolutely great) prompt mathematical sublimity; criterion concerns cognitive limits and the idea of greatness (§25–26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of satisfaction in judgements upon the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the quality of the satisfaction in our judgements upon the Sublime.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublime arouses a mixed feeling (pain and pleasure) tied to recognition of our supersensible capacity; different from peaceful pleasure of beauty (§27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamically Sublime in Nature — nature regarded as might
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of Nature regarded as Might” and the dynamically sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When nature appears as overwhelming power, the judgement is dynamically sublime: the feeling arises from the relation of the subject’s moral/mental capacity to objects of threatening power (§28–29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime awakens feeling of supersensible destination and moral feeling prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeling of the Sublime awakens a feeling of the supersensible destination of man and presupposes moral feeling in man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublime judgments imply recognition of a supersensible vocation and are tied to moral consciousness; Kant links necessary agreement about sublime to moral presuppositions (§—editor’s intro & relevant §§).

rubrics_metrics.name: In sublime judgement pain without fear (horror without fear) is acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: The objects of nature called sublime inspire pain (horror) but must not produce real fear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purity of the sublime experience, the feeling should be an aesthetic horror (awe) not an actual fear that compromises reflective judgement (§editor’s intro discussion of Lucretius).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction and method of aesthetical judgements: no objective principle of taste possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that there is no objective principle of taste possible and that principle of Taste is subjective principle of Judgement in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant argues taste lacks a determinate objective rule; method involves appeal to common sense and reflective principles rather than fixed concepts (§30–36).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective purposiveness of Nature (teleological judgement)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the objective purposiveness of Nature.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teleological judgement assesses organisms and natural systems as if they are purposive; distinguishes formal vs material purposiveness (§61 onward).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal vs material (objective) purposiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the objective purposiveness which is merely formal as distinguished from that which is material.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal purposiveness pertains to how things appear fit with cognitive faculties; material purposiveness refers to genuine adaptation to ends — crucial distinction for teleological evaluation (§62).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative vs inner purposiveness of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the relative, as distinguished from the inner, purposiveness of nature.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative purposiveness concerns external relations and functions; inner purposiveness pertains to internal organization (organisms) — criteria differ accordingly (§63).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organised beings are natural purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: “Things regarded as natural purposes are organised beings.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisms show reciprocal part-whole relations that imply purposiveness; criterion for detecting teleological character in natural entities (§65).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of judging of internal purposiveness in organised beings
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the principle of judging of internal purposiveness in organised beings.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative principle: judge internal organisation by reference to ends and mutual dependence of parts; marks teleological explanation (§66).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleological judging of nature as system of purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the principle of the teleological judging of nature in general as a system of purposes.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We may reflectively construe nature as a purposive ensemble to explain organic interrelations; this is regulative rather than constitutive (§67).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of Teleology as internal principle of natural science
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the principle of Teleology as internal principle of natural science.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant discusses the methodological role of teleology in biology: as a guiding heuristic when mechanistic explanation is insufficient; caution against dogmatic teleology (§68).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antinomy of the Judgement and limits of teleological explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: “What is an antinomy of the Judgement?” and the representation/solution of this antinomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize contradictions when trying to dogmatically assert teleology vs mechanism; the antinomy frames limits of claiming objective purposiveness (§69–76).

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural purpose inexplicable; subordination of mechanism to teleological principle in some explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: “The reason that we cannot treat the concept of a Technic of nature dogmatically is the fact that a natural purpose is inexplicable” and “Of the necessary subordination of the mechanical to the teleological principle in the explanation of a thing as a natural purpose.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant holds that in explaining organisms one sometimes must subordinate mechanistic accounts to teleological principles as regulative aids; but teleology cannot be dogmatically postulated as a constitutive law (§74, §80).

rubrics_metrics.name: Association of mechanism with teleological principle in explanation of natural product
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the association of mechanism with the teleological principle in the explanation of a natural purpose as a natural product.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good explanations may combine mechanical laws with teleological functional analysis; evaluate whether explanation appropriately integrates both without illicitly converting regulative teleology into constitutive law (§81).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleological system in external relations of organised beings and ultimate purpose of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the teleological system in the external relations of organised beings” and “Of the ultimate purpose of nature as a teleological system.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess claims about systemic teleology (ecosystemic or global purposes) with Kant’s caution: teleological readings are reflective, heuristic, and not necessarily metaphysical facts (§82–83).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physico-theology and ethico-theology; moral proof of the Being of God
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections on Physico-theology, Ethico-theology, and the moral proof of the Being of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant examines theological inferences from teleology and from morality; important criteria: limitations of physico-theology and conditions under which moral practical reason supports faith claims (§85–91).
